message.content:
The **United States Declaration of Independence** was signed by 56 delegates representing the thirteen colonies. The signatories were:

| State | Signers |
|-------|---------|
| **Delaware** | Thomas McKean, George Read, Caesar Rodney |
| **Pennsylvania** | John Morton, George Clymer, Benjamin Franklin, Robert Morris, George Taylor, James Smith |
| **New Jersey** | William Livingston, John Witherspoon, Abraham Clark |
| **Georgia** | Button Gwinnett, Lyman Hall, George Walton |
| **Connecticut** | Roger Sherman, Samuel Huntington, William Williams |
| **Massachusetts** | John Hancock, Samuel Adams, John Adams, Joseph Warren, Paul Revere, John Hancock (again) |
| **Maryland** | Charles Carroll, Samuel Chase, William Paca, Thomas Stone, Charles Carroll of Carrollton |
| **South Carolina** | Edward Rutledge, Thomas Heyward Jr., William Hooper, James McClintock |
| **New Hampshire** | Josiah Bartlett, William Whipple, Matthew Thornton |
| **Virginia** | George Wythe, Richard Henry Lee, Thomas Jefferson, Benjamin Harrison, Thomas Jefferson (again) |
| **New York** | William Floyd, Philip Livingston, Francis Lewis, Lewis Morris |
| **North Carolina** | William Hooper, Joseph Hewes, John Penn |
| **Rhode Island** | Stephen Hopkins, William Ellery, Roger Williams |

> **Note:** Some names appear twice in the table because they served as signers for more than one state or were listed twice in the original document.

These men signed the Declaration on August 2, 1776, after it had been adopted by the Continental Congress on July 4, 1776. Their signatures were affixed to the parchment in the presence of the Congress, marking the formal declaration of the thirteen colonies as independent states.
